statusLine: The polluted reach went from about 9 km below Nanjangud to 104 km - close to the river's entire Karnataka course - and CPCB files the change under the annexure titled 'PRS wherein improvement was observed'.

statusFacts.label: Polluted stretch
statusFacts.value: Saragur village downstream to the water-supply intake point of T. Narasipura town

statusFacts.label: Length (2025)
statusFacts.value: 104.3 km (Paani Earth mapping). KSPCB puts the river's whole Karnataka course at about 105 km (action plan, p.3).

statusFacts.label: Classification
statusFacts.value: Priority V - CPCB's mildest band - on a worst BOD of 6 mg/L (CPCB 2025, pp.15 and 77)

statusFacts.label: Worst monitored point
statusFacts.value: The T. Narasipura water-supply intake: 6 mg/L in the 2022-23 round and 6 mg/L again in 2024 - the highest of the five stations on the stretch, at the point a town draws its drinking water (CPCB 2025, pp.48 and 144)

statusFacts.label: Towns on the stretch
statusFacts.value: Three town boundaries touch the mapped 2025 reach - Sargur (TP), Nanjangud (CMC) and T. Narasipura (TMC). The monthly progress reports itemise only Nanjangud.

statusFacts.label: Restoration target
statusFacts.value: Reduce BOD below 3 mg/L to meet the Primary Water Quality Criteria for Bathing Water (organised outdoor bathing)

growthNote: CPCB's earlier lists did not carry the Kabini at all: the 1993-94 and 2011 stretch sets in the same partner package are Cauvery, Bhavani, Lakshmanthirtha and Tamil Nadu reaches, with nothing on this river. It first appears in 2018 as the short reach below Nanjangud, unchanged in the 2020 mapping, and is redrawn in 2025 to run from Saragur - up near where the river leaves the Kabini reservoir - all the way down to the T. Narasipura intake. The stretch grew upstream and downstream at once, and picked up two more towns doing so. Only the 2025 reach is drawn on the map. The 2018 length shown is KSPCB's own, about 9 km from the Nanjangud water-supply intake to Hejjige village (action plan, p.3); Paani Earth's mapping of the 2018 edition covers about 3 km of that and her separately-labelled 2020 lines are geometrically identical to it, so drawing one would understate the reach by two thirds.
priorityNote: Priority is CPCB's BOD-based band, set by the worst monitoring point on the stretch: I is above 30 mg/L, V is 3-6. On that scale the Kabini moved from IV to V, which is why it sits in CPCB's list of stretches where improvement was observed against 2018 (Annexure X, p.108) - even though the reach CPCB now names is more than ten times longer. The documents do not sit easily together either: the KSPCB action plan heads the stretch 'Priority: IV (BOD 6-10 mg/L)' while giving its own BOD range as 3.6-6.5 mg/L, which is mostly the Priority V band (p.3).
bodCaveat: What Priority V means here: the worst of the five monitored points read 6 mg/L, the top of the 3-6 band. It is the mildest CPCB category - and every station on the stretch is still above 3 mg/L, the bathing-water criterion, including the one at Saragur at the very head of it. Priority is set from BOD alone, on grab samples, so a reading reflects dilution as much as load: the CWC gauge at T. Narasipur on this map records a water-year mean of 51.9 cumec in 2023-24 against a 199.3 cumec long-term average, and the same effluent in a year like that reads worse. BOD also says nothing about metals or pesticides, which no public monitoring we hold reports on this river.
mprOverview: Tracked under NGT order OA 673/2018 through monthly NMCG progress reports. Through the August 2025 edition those reports carried a stretch-wise section for the Kabini, and it named one town: Nanjangud. From October 2025 the per-stretch narrative disappears, and by April 2026 the report is state-wide annexure tables only - station classes and STP lists.
levelCoverage: Sewage and solid waste are reported at ULB (town) level, and only for Nanjangud. Sargur and T. Narasipura - the towns at either end of the 2025 stretch - appear in the Mysuru District Environment Plan (May 2022) but in no MPR edition. Industrial effluent is reported as a taluk-wide compliance count, not per estate or per unit. Nothing is reported at gram-panchayat level for the rural reach between the towns.
reportingCaveat: Figures here are what the official documents (CPCB reports, NMCG MPRs, the KSPCB action plan, District Environment Plans) report. Where something shows as nil, not submitted, or unmentioned, it means it is not recorded in those documents - it may still be present or happening on the ground, or held in non-public records.

tabs.label: Sewage
tabs.source: NMCG Monthly Progress Reports (Karnataka, Kabini stretch, to August 2025; STP annexure April 2026); Revised District Environmental Plan of Mysuru District (May 2022); KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini
tabs.intro: When the stretch was the 9 km below Nanjangud, one town sat on it and the reports covered that town. The 2025 stretch runs past three. Sargur, at the head of it, has no sewage treatment at all and none listed as planned; T. Narasipura, at the foot of it, is where the worst BOD on the river is measured - and neither appears in any progress report.

units.name: Nanjangud (CMC)
units.caveat: The town's sewage is reported at 8.72 MLD in the KSPCB action plan (p.6) but 5.41 MLD in the 2022 DEP and every MPR since. Nothing in the documents explains the difference; the lower figure is charted here because it is the one the reporting chain has used since.
units.generationNote: 5.414796 MLD in the DEP (2022) and repeated in the MPRs through August 2025.
units.capacity: 7 MLD operational; an upgraded 8 MLD plant at Goluru got consent to establish on 31/07/2025 (CTE-349927, valid to 2030) and is listed operational and complying in the April 2026 annexure.
units.gapNote: still untreated at the April 2026 utilisation of 3.5 MLD; the network, not the plant, is the bottleneck

infrastructure.label: Rs 36.86 crore UGD DPR - 'under completion stage'
infrastructure.status: Completion timeline still printed as 31-03-2021 in every edition for four years

infrastructure.label: Household connections
infrastructure.status: 40% of the town on UGD in the action plan, 50% in the 2022 DEP, 60% by the August 2025 MPR

infrastructure.label: 8 MLD SBT upgrade at Goluru
infrastructure.status: Consent to establish 31/07/2025; operational and complying, April 2026 annexure

infrastructure.label: Rs 80 crore restoration cost (action plan, section 6 and Table-3)
infrastructure.status: Rs 2.5 crore per MLD of capital cost for primary, secondary and tertiary treatment, asked for as Rs 80 crore of budgetary provision: Rs 1.18 crore a year of O&M for the existing 7 MLD STP plus Rs 78.82 crore for UGD to the 60% of the town still uncovered and house connections for the whole of it. Every rupee is Nanjangud - Sargur and T. Narasipura, both on the 2025 stretch, are not costed - and the table is headed 'Cost Component involved in the Rejuvenation of Polluted Stretch of Bhadra', another river's name left in the Kabini plan.

units.level: ULB (Town Municipal Council) - one DEP snapshot
units.mprNote: Not itemised in any MPR edition, though the stretch now ends at this town's water-supply intake.

units.generationNote: The plan's own figure for the town; UGD covers 50% of its area.

tabs.label: Industrial effluent
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini, section 2.5; NMCG Monthly Progress Report, August 2025
tabs.intro: The Nanjangud industrial belt sits at the head of the original polluted reach. Both the action plan and the progress reports report it as discharging nothing to the river.
tabs.summaryLine: Zero-discharge asserted for 140 units; no public effluent data exists to check it against

categories.label: The zero-discharge position
categories.body: The action plan states that every industry in Nanjangud taluk has an effluent or sewage treatment plant, that treated water is used on land for gardening inside the premises, and that 'No industries in the Nanjangudu taluk are discharging the effluents ... into the river' (section 2.5).
points: Units by KSPCB category in the plan's table: 29 Red, 17 Orange, 84 Green, 10 White - 140 in all.
Named Red-category activity includes a beer manufacturer, 2 organic chemicals, 2 pharmaceuticals, 4 pulp and paper, sugar and distillery, synthetic fibre and 3 textile units.
The August 2025 MPR reports 38 water-polluting industries, 9.03 MLD of effluent and 38 ETPs of 9.43 MLD capacity, all recorded as complying; CETP nil at every status.
The KIADB Thandya and Adakanahalli estates are not named in the August 2025 stretch section at all.

categories.label: What would let anyone check it
categories.body: The zero-discharge position is the board's own assertion. For a sugar, distillery, pulp-and-paper and pharmaceutical cluster upstream of a polluted stretch, no published effluent data exists to test it: there is no public OCEMS-style feed for these units, and the compliance table reports a count, not a measurement.

tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini, section 2.2; NMCG Monthly Progress Report, August 2025; Revised District Environmental Plan of Mysuru District (May 2022)
tabs.intro: Municipal solid waste generated vs processed (tonnes/day) and the processing and landfill infrastructure, for the towns along the stretch. Bank dumping is one of the few pollution sources the action plan names outright. It is also the one with no closure status in any report since.
tabs.summaryLine: Plan records dumping on the banks; no edition since says it stopped

infrastructure.label: Dumping on the river banks
infrastructure.status: The action plan records that 'apart from dumping the solid wastes in the MSW site, some quantity is also dumped on banks of the river' (section 2.2); its remedy is disposal only at MSW sites. No edition since reports whether it stopped.

infrastructure.label: Sanitary landfill
infrastructure.status: Rs 5.16 crore DPR approved, construction 'in progress'; the proposed-facility timeline is still printed as 31.03.2021.

infrastructure.label: Collection and segregation
infrastructure.status: Door-to-door collection in all 31 wards; source segregation in 24 of them, against the DEP's count of 31 of 31.

tabs.label: Hazardous waste
tabs.source: NMCG Monthly Progress Reports (Karnataka, Kabini stretch, to August 2025); Revised District Environmental Plan of Mysuru District (May 2022)
tabs.summaryLine: No hazardous-waste figure reported for the stretch in any edition held

categories.label: Hazardous waste
categories.body: Hazardous waste is not reported for this stretch.
points: No hazardous-waste generation, treatment or TSDF figure appears in any NMCG progress report edition for the Kabini stretch through August 2025.

The Mysuru District Environment Plan (May 2022) inventories solid waste, domestic sewage, industrial wastewater, air, mining and noise; no known public hazardous-waste inventory covers the district's Kabini-side towns.
Biomedical waste is the one special stream reported here, and only for Nanjangud - see Solid waste.

tabs.label: FSTP
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini; NMCG Monthly Progress Reports (to August 2025); Revised District Environmental Plan of Mysuru District (May 2022)
tabs.summaryLine: No faecal-sludge plant on the stretch; the unsewered share's septage route is unreported

categories.label: FSTP
categories.body: Faecal-sludge treatment for the unsewered load:
points: Faecal sludge and septage do not appear in the KSPCB Kabini action plan.

With 40% of Nanjangud's households unconnected to the UGD, their septage route is not reported in any edition through August 2025 - the unsewered share's septage is the unaccounted flow between the town and the river.
Sargur has no sewerage network and no facility marked as planned; T. Narasipura's UGD covers half the town. No faecal-sludge plant is reported for either.
The Mysuru District Environment Plan lists an FSTP approved for HD Kote, a Kabini-side town off the 2025 stretch; no plant is reported operational anywhere on the stretch itself.

tabs.label: E-flow
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini, Table-4; India-WRIS Dataset API (CWC discharge at T. Narasipur)
tabs.intro: The action plan has an environmental-flow section. It tabulates two years of flow and stops there.
tabs.summaryLine: Two years of min/max flow tabulated; no e-flow requirement set for the river

categories.label: What the plan says
categories.body: Table-4 gives flow at the T. Narasipura hydrological observation site for two years: 2015, minimum 7.688 and maximum 388.428 m3/s; 2016, minimum 8.928 and maximum 37.684 m3/s. No environmental-flow requirement is set, no season is distinguished, and no agency is named against one.
points: The plan's short- and long-term action tables carry no e-flow item.

The Kabini dam sits just above the head of the stretch, and the Nugu and Taraka dams control two of its tributaries; how much water is released from any of them, and when, is not reported in any document here.

categories.label: What the gauge shows
categories.body: The CWC station at T. Narasipur on this map carries a fuller record than the plan's two years - 2,990 days of observed discharge between January 2015 and March 2026. Tap it for the full series.
points: Water-year mean discharge swings from 8.7 cumec in 2014-15 and 51.9 in 2023-24 to 1,072 in 2018-19, against a long-term average of 199.3 cumec.
Priority bands are set on BOD from grab samples, so a dry year and a wet year of the same effluent load do not read the same.
Discharge is published in arrears; the telemetric level feed has been frozen at source since 04 June 2026.

tabs.label: Treated-water reuse
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini, section 2.5; NMCG Monthly Progress Reports (to August 2025; STP annexure April 2026)
tabs.summaryLine: Industrial on-land gardening is the only reuse reported; no municipal reuse in any edition

categories.label: Treated-water reuse
categories.body: Reuse of treated water as reported for this stretch:
points: The action plan reports that industries in Nanjangud taluk use their treated water on land for gardening inside their premises (section 2.5). No volume is given, and the statement covers the taluk rather than named units.

No municipal treated-water reuse is reported for Nanjangud, Sargur or T. Narasipura in any edition through August 2025. Nanjangud's 7 MLD plant is reported at 2 MLD utilised in August 2025 and 3.5 MLD in April 2026, but where the treated water goes is not reported.

tabs.label: Flood plain
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Kabini; NMCG Monthly Progress Reports (Karnataka, Kabini stretch, to August 2025)
tabs.summaryLine: No flood-plain-zone commitment in the plan or in any progress report edition held

categories.label: Flood plain
categories.body: The flood plain does not appear as an obligation in this stretch's record.
points: No flood-plain-zone commitment - notification, encroachment check, plantation, or a prohibition on dumping in the zone - appears in the KSPCB Kabini action plan or in any MPR edition through August 2025 in what we hold.

The plan's named executing agencies cover sewerage and solid waste (CMC Nanjangud), monitoring and consent (KSPCB), and the bathing ghat and offerings in the river (the temple authority at Nanjangud). The river's banks appear only as the place solid waste is dumped (section 2.2).
The 2025 stretch runs 104 km past three towns and a largely rural reach; no encroachment count, demarcation or plantation figure exists for any of it in the documents here.

grievance.label: Report illegal sewage or effluent discharge
grievance.sub: NMCG's online grievance module, set up on NGT direction and operational since January 2021. State chief secretaries are the accountable authority.

keyTerms.note: A river stretch where BOD exceeds 3 mg/L, the Primary Water Quality Criteria for Bathing Water. CPCB identifies them nationally and states must produce restoration action plans for each.
Sets the classification and publishes the national polluted-stretch list; the October 2025 edition is the current one.
Writes and executes the state's river action plans, monitors water quality, and issues industrial consents.
The monthly report each state files with NMCG under NGT OA 673/2018 on restoring its polluted stretches.

keyTerms.full: National Green Tribunal, Original Application 673 of 2018
keyTerms.note: The order that made polluted-stretch restoration a monitored, monthly-reported obligation with the chief secretary answerable.
Oxygen consumed by microbes breaking down organic matter, in mg/L. High BOD means heavy organic load - typically sewage - or too little flow to dilute it.
I is worst: a maximum BOD above 30 mg/L. II is 20-30, III is 10-20, IV is 6-10, V is 3-6. The band is set by the worst monitoring point on the stretch.
The CPCB and state-board station network whose readings feed the classification.
CPCB's use-based classification: A is drinking water with disinfection only, C is drinking after conventional treatment, D is wildlife and fisheries, E is irrigation and industrial cooling.
The sewer network. An STP only treats what the network delivers to it, which is why coverage matters as much as capacity.

keyTerms.full: Effluent Treatment Plant / Common Effluent Treatment Plant
keyTerms.note: A treatment plant inside a single industry, or a shared one serving an industrial estate.

keyTerms.full: City Municipal Council / Town Municipal Council / Town Panchayat
keyTerms.note: Karnataka's urban local bodies by size. The three towns on this stretch are one of each.

evidence.headline: The worst reading on the stretch sits at the point a town draws its drinking water - and the official record has no second opinion.
points: CPCB monitoring, maximum BOD in mg/L (2022-23, then 2024): Kabini at Saragur village D/S 4.0, 4.0; at the causeway, Sattur 4.0, 3.5; u/s the intake to Nanjangud & Gundlupet at Debur 3.5, 3.8; at the bathing ghat, Nanjangud 4.5, 5.0; at the water-supply intake to T. Narasipura 6.0, 6.0. Every station is above 3 mg/L, the Primary Water Quality Criteria for Bathing Water, in both rounds.

The action plan's own Table-2 covers two stations for 2017 and 2018: the bathing ghat at Nanjangud reads Class D in 2017 (BOD 2.4-6.5, faecal coliform 320-790 MPN/100ml) and Class E in 2018; the water-supply intake at T. Narasipura reads Class C in both years (BOD 1.2-3.0, then 1.04-2.0). By CPCB's 2022-23 and 2024 rounds the intake is the worst point on the stretch, not the best.
The plan's own reading of that table: 'The results indicate that the water is polluted due to sewage from Nanjungud Town.'

The classification runs on BOD alone. No known public monitoring reports heavy metals, pesticides or pharmaceutical residues on this river - which matters upstream of a belt that includes distilleries, pulp and paper, and pharmaceutical units.

Everything on this page comes from CPCB, KSPCB, NMCG and the district administration - the bodies being held to account. We hold no independent sampling, no citizen-collected record and no academic study for this stretch. That absence is itself worth stating: on this river, the official record has no second opinion.
